main_text.head: XXIX. IURISPRUDENTIA SACRA.
main_text.p: 5I. Iurisprudentia sacra est doctrina æqui & boni ex sacris literis petita. Et quia ex Mose, divino illo legislatore, colligitur, Mosaica dici potest. Huius iurisprudentiae tanta est dignitas, ut merito habeatur 10pro regulâ & normâ iurisprudentiae Romanæ.Et spes magna me tenet, pios ICtos cunctas leges suas ad ius diuinum per Mosem traditum tandem aliquando reuocaturos, dissimiles Thomae Linacro, qui lecto illo Christi Matth. 5. vers. 44. Diligite inimicos vestros, librum in terram 15proiecit, his verbis additis: Aut hæc vera non sunt, aut Christiani non sumus.
II. Iurisprudentiae sacrae partes sunt duæ: prima, de collatione iuris Romanicum decalogo; 20secunda, de legum Mosaicarum forensium explanatione.
III. Prima pars continetur hac regulâ. Leges iuris Romani referantur ad præcepta decalogi, hoc fere modo.

page.notes: Line numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 are printed in the left margin and are transcribed as notes. The big initial I of the first paragraph is joined to the following "Urisprudentia" as "Iurisprudentia". The run-on lead-in "Adpraceptumprimum." is printed without a space and is copied as printed. Long s is read as plain s throughout (e.g. "est" for "eft", "potest" for "poteft"). Line-end hyphen in "litigan-" is printed and the word continues on the next page; "tium," at the foot right is the catchword. Edge marks at the left and right margins are not transcribed.
